chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Al-Halabi, raising it (to the Prophet), said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Withhold your tongue, for it is a charity by which you give charity upon yourself.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'And a servant will not recognize the reality of faith until he guards his tongue.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of restraining the tongue in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, the Prophet (SAW) elevates the discipline of the tongue from mere restraint to an active act of self-charity (Sadaqah), highlighting its role in spiritual purification. This aligns with Shia scholarly emphasis on 'Hifz al-Lisan' as a prerequisite for the perfection of Iman, linking verbal conduct directly to the depth of one's faith.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Al Halby, raising it,

‘Heasws said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘Withhold your tongue for it is a charity you give charity upon yourself’. Then heasws said: ‘And a servant will not recognise the reality of the Emān until he stores from his tongue’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from al- Halabi in a marfu’ manner from the Messenger of Allah who has said the following: “
Control your tongue; it is a charity that you give to yourself. He then said, ‘A servant (of Allah) will not know the reality of his belief until he reserves (controls) his tongue.’”
